judgments.evidence: src/sim.jl:1661-1663 run _finish! and _tail! in the inner finally, even off a loop-side throw. src/sim.jl:1757 records LoopError. Probe line 42-43 (probe.jl): a Tripwire throw in frame 2 ends with source LoopError and lifecycle errored, after the tail ran (line 48 shows the device's shutdown!).

src/sim.jl:1903-1909 joins every spawned task under one join_timeout deadline and reports a late one by name (DeviceJoinTimeout, src/sim.jl:1934-1939). The same _tail! runs on the abnormal path (src/sim.jl:1663). Probe line 69: HangShutdown is abandoned at the 0.5 s cap with a DeviceJoinTimeout naming 'device 1 (HangShutdown)'.

Probe lines 45-51: StepError.boundary = 1 at t = 0.15, latest(sim) is boundary 1 at t = 0.1, logged boundaries [0, 1], and the device saw no newer boundary. src/sim.jl:1748-1751: publication is a boundary's last act, so the failed boundary published nothing.

src/sim.jl:1894-1903: _tail! calls unblock!(entry.dev) synchronously on the calling task, before it sets the join deadline. Only the joins run under join_timeout. Probe line 69, with join_timeout = 0.5: a shutdown! that sleeps 3 s returns run! in 0.58 s, but an unblock! that sleeps 3 s holds run! for 3.0 s. A hanging shutdown! is bounded because it runs on the device task inside the wrapper (src/devices.jl:664-667). A hanging unblock! is not bounded.
judgments.fix: Bring unblock! under the tail's join_timeout deadline. For example, run each unblock! on its own task and wait for it within the shared deadline, so that a hanging unblock! is reported and abandoned the way a hanging task is.

judgments.evidence: Probe line 59: on an errored simulation, run!, step!, init!, replay!, live!, attach! and detach! are each refused as ServiceLifecycle with status :errored. latest and trace still read. src/sim.jl:598-608 (_assert_advanceable) and src/sim.jl:836-837 (init!) refuse errored.

Probe lines 50-51: logged boundaries are [0, 1], the last consistent boundary. The trace's last record is the batch drained at the top of the failing frame (frame 2, entering from boundary 1), which src/dataplane.jl:496 records at the drain. That frame top is the last consistent boundary, as §13.4 requires for replay. Nothing past it is published.
judgments.note: The trace holds the failing frame's top-drain batch. It is keyed at the last consistent frame top, so the claim holds. A reader could still take 'ends at' more strictly.
